skill.name: debugging-toolkit-smart-debug
skill.description: Structured debugging workflow for triage, observability analysis, root cause investigation, fix planning, and post-fix validation.
skill.summary: Guide agents through evidence-based debugging from first triage to prevention.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: All three static findings were adjudicated as false positives. The external command matches are Markdown backticks or a TypeScript example fence, not executable shell invocation. No prompt injection or semantic abuse evidence was found in SKILL.md.

static_findings.snippet: - If detailed examples are required, open `resources/implementation-playbook.md`.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 24 is a Markdown inline reference to a resource path inside backticks. It is documentation text and does not execute a shell command.
Line 148 starts a TypeScript fenced example block. The surrounding content is illustrative pseudocode and contains no shell execution path.
Lines 135-136 are success criteria that say tests pass and no performance regression. They do not request network scanning or reconnaissance.

content.value_statement: Complex bugs waste time when evidence is scattered across logs, traces, tests, and code. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through structured triage, root cause analysis, fix planning, and validation.
actual_capabilities: Parses error reports for stack traces, affected services, environment, and failure patterns.
Guides triage with ranked hypotheses, probable causes, and debugging strategy.
Recommends observability data to collect from logs, traces, metrics, and error trackers.
Suggests instrumentation points, validation steps, rollback checks, and prevention tasks.
Defines a structured report covering issue summary, root cause, fix proposal, validation, and prevention.
limitations: It does not connect to observability tools or fetch data by itself.
It depends on accurate inputs, logs, traces, and reproduction details from the user.
It cannot guarantee a fix without running tests and validating in the target environment.
Production debugging recommendations still require proper permissions and operational safeguards.

use_cases.title: Production Incident Triage
use_cases.description: An on-call engineer uses the skill to organize symptoms, gather telemetry, and rank likely root causes.

use_cases.title: Intermittent Bug Investigation
use_cases.description: A backend developer uses it to compare logs, traces, and code paths for a failure that is hard to reproduce.

use_cases.title: Fix Validation Planning
use_cases.description: A QA lead uses it to define tests, performance checks, and monitoring steps before a fix is released.

prompt_templates.title: Triage a New Bug
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the smart debug workflow for this issue: [paste error, environment, frequency, and reproduction steps].

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a Stack Trace
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this stack trace and related logs. Identify likely causes, missing evidence, and the next debugging steps.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Observability Queries
prompt_templates.prompt: Given this production symptom, list the logs, traces, metrics, and error tracker views I should inspect first.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a Root Cause and Fix
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this suspected root cause and proposed fix. Provide falsification criteria, regression tests, rollout checks, and prevention steps.

output_examples.input: A checkout endpoint times out for five percent of users in production.
output: Summary: intermittent checkout timeout with direct user impact.
Likely causes: slow payment provider response, sequential database queries, or saturated connection pools.
Next checks: compare traces for slow requests, review payment API latency, and inspect deployment timing.

output_examples.input: A saved workspace crashes a React page after loading.
output: Hypothesis: corrupted saved state, missing null handling, or a schema mismatch during hydration.
Evidence to gather: browser error details, recent schema changes, failing workspace fields, and reproduction steps.
Validation plan: add a regression fixture, test migration handling, and verify fallback rendering.

best_practices: Start with the smallest reproducible case before changing implementation details.
Tie each hypothesis to evidence, falsification criteria, and a verification step.
Record the root cause and add monitoring or tests that catch the same failure.
anti_patterns: Changing code before confirming the failure mode and impact.
Treating AI hypotheses as facts without logs, traces, tests, or user reports.
Adding broad production logging without sampling, access controls, or privacy review.

faq.question: Does this skill run debugging commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides a workflow and recommendations for investigation, testing, and validation.

faq.question: Can it replace incident response procedures?
faq.answer: No. Use it alongside established escalation, access, and change management processes.

faq.question: Which tools does it mention?
faq.answer: It references common error tracking, APM, tracing, logging, profiling, and browser debugging tools.

faq.question: Is it useful for local bugs?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports local reproduction, stack trace analysis, breakpoints, and regression test planning.

faq.question: Can it diagnose production issues without telemetry?
faq.answer: It can structure the investigation, but reliable diagnosis requires logs, traces, metrics, or clear reproduction details.

faq.question: How should sensitive data be handled?
faq.answer: Redact secrets and personal data before sharing logs, traces, screenshots, or customer context.
